provenance.instrument: City of Bradford Zoning Ordinance (Code Chapter 220 Zoning, Ord. No. 3231 of 6-23-2009, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 BR1254, City of Bradford, McKean County (220-8 'County': 'McKean County, Pennsylvania'). The code was adopted as a whole by Ord. No. 3296 of 5-14-2024. Each district article states its authorized uses and its area and bulk rules as web text. The zoning map and three appendix figures are PDF attachments and were not opened. Floodplain rules are Chapter 114 Floodplain Management
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 version shown: 'Code 2026-08-11'. New Laws lists no legislation awaiting codification (0)
checks: ADU: the code has no accessory dwelling unit term. A 'Guesthouse', defined as 'A small, separate house on the grounds of a larger one, used for accommodating guests' (220-8, added 3-26-2019 by Ord. No. 3231.2), is an accessory use by special exception in R-1, R-2 and R-3, and a principal use by special exception in C-1 and C-2 (220-23B(2)(e), 220-31B(2)(e), 220-39B(2)(e), 220-55B(1)(j), 220-64B(1)(j)). Article XIII gives it no specific standards, so the general special exception standards of 220-89 apply

A guesthouse is read here as the code's detached ADU form. The code does not say whether it may be rented as a separate home, how small it must be, or whether the owner must live on the lot. Ask the zoning officer
Parking: 'Guesthouse: 1 space for each apartment in addition to 2 spaces required for the existing dwelling' (220-114C). Any fraction of a space counts as one (220-114A)

Accessory structures in C-D, R-1, R-2 and R-3: 'one story, but no more than 20 feet'. Accessory buildings and roofed projections may cover at most 30% of a required rear yard (40% on a corner lot) in R-1, R-2 and R-3 (220-94C(7)(b)). Detached garages and storage structures stay out of the required front yard, 5 ft from a side line, 3 ft from a rear line and 10 ft from the dwelling (220-94C(7)(a)). The code gives no accessory yards for a guesthouse, so the district yards are read as the safe figures

Uses: in C-D, R-1, R-2 and R-3 'any use not specifically listed as an authorized use in the zoning district shall not be permitted' (220-12B). In C-1, C-2, M-1 and M-2 a use not listed may be allowed as a comparable use by special exception if it is of the same general character as a listed use (220-12C, 220-90I). A single-family or two-family dwelling must be the only principal structure on its lot (220-12D)

Conversion apartment: a unit created inside an existing single-family dwelling is a special exception in R-2 (one new unit) and R-3 (up to four), at least 400 sq ft each, with one added parking space. Detached garages and other accessory structures may not be converted to dwelling units under this listing (220-90J)
Two-family dwellings: a special exception in R-2 on a 10,000 sq ft site, 5,000 sq ft per unit (220-90CC), and permitted by right in R-3 on 4,000 sq ft (220-39, 220-40)
Lots of record: a lot of record may be built on with a use the district permits though it is below the area and width minimums, if it meets the yards, height and coverage (220-125A)

Floodplain (Chapter 114, FIRM of 12-22-2016): a permit for any construction or development. In a floodway no new construction or development without an engineering analysis of no rise and a DEP permit. In an AE area without a floodway nothing within 50 ft landward of the top of bank without a DEP permit (114-18B(2)(b)). New construction and substantial improvement of a residential structure have the lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation. An accessory structure that is not elevated may not be used for human habitation and may have at most 200 sq ft (114-23E)
Rooming houses are also a special exception in R-1, R-2, R-3, C-1 and C-2 (added 2019). They are not dwelling units for one household and are not read as an ADU path
provenance.notes: Zoning office: City of Bradford Zoning Officer. Read in a browser on eCode360 (print view and code searches), one page at a time, on 2026-11-18. Read in full: 220-9 to 220-13, 220-14 to 220-62 (C-D, R-1, R-2, R-3, M-C and C-1 articles), 220-63 to 220-70 (C-2), 220-87 to 220-90W, 220-90CC, 220-112 to 220-115, 220-122 to 220-126, 114-23, and 220-8 from A to 'Lot area'. Read in part: 220-8 'Lot coverage' and later lot terms (screenshot), M-1 and M-2 use lists (in-page search only), 220-94 (screenshots), 220-131 to 220-133, 114-16 to 114-18. Not read: 220-0 to 220-7, the rest of 220-8, 220-73 to 220-78 and 220-81 to 220-86 (M-1 and M-2 area and bulk), 220-90X to BB except part of BB, 220-90DD, 220-91 to 220-93, 220-95 to 220-111, 220-116 to 220-121, 220-127 to 220-130, 220-134 to 220-149, Chapter 114 except the sections named, Chapter 191 (subdivision and land development) and the zoning map. Searched the code for accessory dwelling, in-law, accessory apartment, garage apartment, second dwelling, ECHO, extended family, household employee, elder cottage, tenant house, supplemental dwelling, temporary dwelling, apartment addition, living quarters, caretaker, conversion, care of, guest house, two-family and accessory building. Open points: whether a guesthouse is a dwelling unit an owner may rent as a separate home or only a house for guests, whether a guesthouse takes the garage yards of 220-94C(7) or the district's principal yards, whether a guesthouse may be added over a garage, and whether the C-1 and C-2 listing reaches a lot with a house.

path.note: 'Guesthouse' under Uses by special exception, Accessory uses. The Zoning Hearing Board decides after a public hearing on the general standards of 220-89

unlisted_use_scope.quote: Uses of the same general character as any of the uses authorized as permitted uses by right or uses by special exception in the zoning district in which the property is located

value.name: Conversion apartment (R-2, R-3)
value.conditions: A dwelling unit created inside an existing single-family dwelling, by special exception from the Zoning Hearing Board. Each unit at least 400 sq ft of gross floor area with its own living, sleeping, kitchen and sanitary facilities. In R-2 only one new unit in a single-family dwelling, in R-3 up to four. Detached garages and other accessory structures may not be converted to dwelling units. One parking space for each apartment besides the 2 for the house

requires.condition: An existing single-family dwelling to adapt

value.name: Two-family dwelling (R-2)
value.conditions: A building with two dwelling units, by special exception. 'The minimum site required to develop two-family dwellings shall be 10,000 square feet' and 5,000 sq ft per dwelling unit. A two-family dwelling made inside an existing single-family dwelling meets the conversion apartment rules. Two parking spaces per unit
value.note: The single-family or two-family dwelling must be the only principal structure on the lot (220-12D), so a new two-family building takes the place of the house

value.name: Two-family dwelling (R-3)
value.conditions: A building with two dwelling units is a permitted use. 4,000 sq ft and 40 ft wide, front 20 ft, side 4 ft, rear 20 ft or the building height, coverage 60%. Two parking spaces per unit
value.note: The single-family or two-family dwelling must be the only principal structure on the lot (220-12D). Whether an existing house may be turned into two units by right here, or only as a conversion apartment by special exception, is not settled

value.name: Infill housing (R-1, R-2, R-3)
value.conditions: Newly built single-family or two-family dwellings, or townhouses of up to four units, on a lot where deteriorated dwelling units stood before they were demolished. A lot below the district minimum may be used if 75% of the yards can be met. Design compatible with the houses on the same block

requires.condition: Deteriorated dwelling units stood on the lot and were demolished

value.note: C-2 permits infill housing by right (220-64A(1)(zzz))

building_types.note: The guesthouse stands 'on the grounds of a larger one'. The definition does not name a house type

lot_area_per_unit_sqft.note: The R districts give a lot area by dwelling type, not per unit, and say nothing of a guesthouse

districts_read_no_listing.note: M-C, M-1 and M-2 list no dwelling and no guesthouse

districts_in_doubt.note: C-1 and C-2 list a guesthouse as a principal use by special exception but do not authorize single-family dwellings, while a guesthouse stands on the grounds of a larger house

value.condition: A guesthouse is 'A small, separate house on the grounds of a larger one, used for accommodating guests'. The code sets no size, owner or tenant rule for it, and whether it may be let as a home of its own is not settled.

In an identified floodplain area (Chapter 114) every construction or development needs a floodplain permit. In a floodway no new construction, substantial improvement or other development is allowed unless an engineering analysis shows no rise in flood levels, and no new construction or development without a DEP permit. In an AE area without a floodway the work may not raise flood levels more than one foot. New construction and substantial improvement of a residential structure need the lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation.

In an AE area without a floodway 'No new construction or development shall be located within the area measured 50 feet landward from the top-of-bank of any watercourse, unless the appropriate permit is obtained from the Department of Environmental Protection Regional Office'.

In an identified floodplain area an accessory structure that is not elevated or floodproofed 'shall not be designed or used for human habitation', may have no sanitary facilities or fixed utility equipment and at most 200 sq ft of floor area. A larger one below the base flood elevation needs a variance and a recorded nonconversion agreement.

disputed_by.note: The rule is for accessory structures that are not elevated or floodproofed. A guesthouse built with its lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation, as 114-23A asks of residential structures, may not be reached
